microtheory.name: vision_foundation
microtheory.definition: Vision as the substrate's foundational visual-perception vocabulary. The substrate has a vision.py module but no Mt explaining what vision IS — light, optics, retina, edges, motion, depth, color, objects, scenes. This Mt provides that grounding. Substrate analogue: the input domain for substrate's visual cortex equivalent (the existing ventral_visual_stream concept in neuro_sensory_cortex Mt maps here).

concepts.name: light
concepts.definition: Electromagnetic radiation in visible range ~380-780 nm. Photons. Substrate analogue: substrate's visual input medium.

concepts.name: wavelength_visible
concepts.definition: Determines color. 400nm = violet, 700nm = red. Substrate analogue: substrate's color channel parameter.

concepts.name: luminance
concepts.definition: Photometric measure of light intensity, weighted by eye sensitivity. cd/m². Substrate analogue: substrate's brightness channel.

concepts.name: reflectance
concepts.definition: Fraction of light reflected by surface. Determines surface lightness. Substrate analogue: substrate's surface-property estimate.

concepts.name: illuminance
concepts.definition: Light falling on surface. Substrate analogue: substrate's environmental-light estimate.

concepts.name: retina
concepts.definition: Light-sensing layer at back of eye. Rods (low-light, achromatic) + cones (color, daylight) + ganglion cells. Substrate analogue: substrate's visual input transducer.

concepts.name: fovea
concepts.definition: Central retina, high cone density, color vision, highest acuity. ~2° of visual field. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-resolution central attention.

concepts.name: periphery_visual
concepts.definition: Off-center retina. Rod-dominated. Motion + low-light, low resolution + no color. Substrate analogue: substrate's coarse-grain peripheral monitor.

concepts.name: optic_nerve
concepts.definition: Ganglion cell axons from retina to brain. Blind spot at exit. Substrate analogue: substrate's visual-pipeline bottleneck.

concepts.name: lateral_geniculate_nucleus
concepts.definition: LGN. Visual thalamic relay. Magnocellular (motion) + parvocellular (form/color) layers. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-cortical visual gate.

concepts.name: primary_visual_cortex_v1
concepts.definition: V1, occipital lobe. Retinotopic map, edge detectors. Substrate analogue: substrate's primary visual processor.

concepts.name: receptive_field_visual
concepts.definition: Region of visual field a neuron responds to. Substrate analogue: substrate's visual concept's responsive region.

concepts.name: retinotopy_visual
concepts.definition: V1's organization preserves retinal topology. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatially-organized visual Mt.

concepts.name: cortical_magnification_factor
concepts.definition: Fovea hugely over-represented in V1 (50% for 2° of visual field). Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-weighted resolution.

concepts.name: visual_pathway_hierarchy
concepts.definition: V1 → V2 → V4 → IT (ventral, what) + V1 → V2 → V5/MT → parietal (dorsal, where). Substrate analogue: substrate's visual genlMt hierarchy.

concepts.name: ventral_stream_what
concepts.definition: Object identity pathway. Builds invariant object representations. Substrate analogue: substrate's object-recognition Mt chain.

concepts.name: dorsal_stream_where
concepts.definition: Spatial location + action pathway. Motion + space. Substrate analogue: substrate's location + action concept chain.

concepts.name: edge
concepts.definition: Discontinuity in luminance, color, texture, or depth. Substrate analogue: substrate's primary feature.

concepts.name: orientation_visual
concepts.definition: Direction of edge. V1 simple cells tuned to orientation. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge-orientation concept.

concepts.name: spatial_frequency
concepts.definition: Cycles per degree of visual angle. Low = blurry; high = sharp detail. Substrate analogue: substrate's scale-of-detail channel.

concepts.name: color
concepts.definition: Perceptual correlate of wavelength. Three dimensions: hue, saturation, brightness. Substrate analogue: substrate's chromatic channel.

concepts.name: texture
concepts.definition: Statistical pattern over surface. Roughness, regularity. Substrate analogue: substrate's surface-statistics concept.

concepts.name: depth
concepts.definition: Distance from viewer. Multiple cues. Substrate analogue: substrate's 3D-distance estimate.

concepts.name: motion_visual
concepts.definition: Change of position over time. Velocity vectors. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-change feature.

concepts.name: object
concepts.definition: Bounded perceptual unit. Coherent across viewpoints + transformations. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-entity Concept.

concepts.name: object_recognition
concepts.definition: Identifying object class from sensory input. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-from-features matching.

concepts.name: viewpoint_invariance
concepts.definition: Recognising same object from different views. Substrate analogue: substrate's perspective-invariant Concept.

concepts.name: object_permanence_visual
concepts.definition: Knowing object exists when occluded. Develops ~8mo. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-Mt state through input gaps.

concepts.name: scene
concepts.definition: Spatial arrangement of objects in environment. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional spatial Mt.

concepts.name: gist
concepts.definition: Rapid scene category recognition (~100ms). Beach, forest, street. Substrate analogue: substrate's coarse-classification fast path.

concepts.name: spatial_relations
concepts.definition: Above, below, beside, behind. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-relation edges.

concepts.name: context
concepts.definition: Surrounding scene biases object recognition. Toaster in kitchen vs forest. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned Concept activation.

concepts.name: gestalt_grouping
concepts.definition: Wertheimer 1923. Proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, common fate. Perception organizes features into wholes. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional concept emergence.

concepts.name: figure_ground
concepts.definition: Separating foreground object from background. Substrate analogue: substrate's salient-vs-background segmentation.

concepts.name: perceptual_constancy
concepts.definition: Stable perception despite varying input. Size, shape, color, lightness constancies. Substrate analogue: substrate's invariant Concept under transformation.

concepts.name: visual_attention
concepts.definition: Selective processing of subset of visual input. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-priority on visual concepts.

concepts.name: saccade
concepts.definition: Rapid eye movement (~30ms) to bring fovea to a new location. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-shift mechanism.

concepts.name: fixation
concepts.definition: Period between saccades. ~200ms. Substrate analogue: substrate's sustained-attention dwell.

concepts.name: smooth_pursuit
concepts.definition: Slow eye movement tracking moving target. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous-attention tracking.

rules.name: visual_hierarchy_builds_invariance
rules.head: the substrate's visual pipeline processes input from V1 upward
rules.body: each level builds invariance to nuisance variables (position, scale, viewpoint). High-level neurons respond invariantly to object identity. Substrate's hierarchical abstraction.

rules.name: cortical_magnification_reflects_behavioural_importance
rules.head: the substrate allocates visual processing resources
rules.body: behaviourally important regions (fovea) get disproportionate cortex. Substrate's attention-weighted allocation.

rules.name: context_biases_object_recognition
rules.head: the substrate recognises an object
rules.body: scene context primes consistent categories + suppresses inconsistent ones. Substrate's context-conditioned Concept activation.

rules.name: gestalt_grouping_organizes_features
rules.head: the substrate processes multiple visual features
rules.body: it groups them by proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, common fate. Substrate's compositional emergence.

rules.name: saccades_redirect_high_acuity_processing
rules.head: the substrate's peripheral vision detects something interesting
rules.body: a saccade brings the fovea + high-acuity processing to that location. Substrate's attention-redirect mechanism.
